lines: Episode 399 (2026-10-07). The host opens with audio from an X Space in which Blake Neff, attacking her character, says she would "hate Erika for murdering Charlie"; another participant says he meant "marrying" and Neff says he is pretty sure he said marrying. The host calls it a Freudian slip, recalls Andrew Kolvet's early "processing their guilt" remark that Megyn Kelly corrected to grief, and plays a Wear Forbidden parody video. She rebuts Neff's claims about how she treats staff and says his outbursts follow episodes that make Turning Point USA nervous.

The longest segment follows up the previous day's Monster Lab / Elephant Clipping episode. The host says the clip files for Erika Kirk and TPUSA came from Blake Wynn's Las Vegas firm, which has an imprint in Romania, and credits a commentator with the theory that Wynn's orbit supplied Erika's "Kirk Force 1" sneakers, playing a video message about sneakers sent to Charlie. She says the Monster Lab site is now blocked in the United States but visible via VPN. She corrects her earlier identification of the operator ("Mat Servius") and, per Latvian emailers, names him as Matiss Tabuns of Talsi, Latvia. She says Clip It LLC was filed in Wyoming on May 28, 2025 through a registered agent she identifies as Cindy Jackson, whom she ties to the Pandora Papers through a 2022 article about registered agents serving oligarchs, including a company linked to Igor Kolomoisky.

After the break, the host reports, citing emails from UVU staff she says she confirmed, that UVU Police Chief Jeff Long has resigned, and that emergency management director Robin Ebmeyer (transcribed "Ebmyer"/"Edmire") is resigning or has resigned; she says she does not know whether either was forced out. She replays Brian Harpole's Shawn Ryan account and a clip of Andrew Kolvet about the "I got you covered" text, alleges TPUSA misrepresented that message for a year, and reads independent review passages on Maycee Crofts' venue and ticketing preferences and Ebmeyer's absence on September 10. Closing segments mock a Laura Loomer DMV-flag tweet and a Gary Melton / Ian Carroll exchange, read viewer comments (Kolvet's "guilt" remark, a "grieving widow" trademark, a "heavy hitters" quote), ask for tips on Tabuns, and mention the host's late pregnancy.

- MISTRANSCRIPTION: "Tyler Bowyer" -> "Tyler Bowyer" (00:46:42) source: nodes.tsv N-11
- MISTRANSCRIPTION: "Blake Wynn" -> "Blake Wynn" (00:22:20) source: nodes.tsv N-352
- MISTRANSCRIPTION: "Matiss" -> "Matiss" (00:19:10, 00:44:50, 00:45:05) source: host spells the name at 00:14:33

- Unresolved name: "Matiss Tabuns" – the host spells the surname T-A-B-U-N-S; a web search found no confirming coverage. Kept as spoken. Possibly the same individual previously recorded as N-351 Matt Servius; the host now says that name was wrong. Integrator should decide whether to merge or relink.
- Unresolved name: "Christine Fekete" (@what.the.fekete) – not confirmed by web search; kept as transcribed.
- Unresolved place: "Sky Steel" (00:11:45, in the sneaker video) – possibly Scottsdale; kept as transcribed.
- Unresolved term: "TPO say official" (00:32:00, Kolvet clip) – unclear; not used in claims.

- Speaker identity: the sneaker video at 00:11:45 is not identified on air as Blake Wynn; the host frames it in his context. The 00:31:55 clip is introduced by the host as Kolvet but the speaker is not named in the clip.

- Number discrepancy: the host says the registered agent runs "nearly 3,000 businesses" (00:16:35), while the 2022 article she reads says "more than 350 companies" (00:19:52). She also calls the agent 82 years old, and the article gave 77 at the time.
- Revises link C-13988 -> C-13901: the host explicitly says her prior-day name for the operator was wrong. Integrator may drop it if C-13901 is read as being only about the role.
- Artifacts referenced but not shown: The Atlantic article (00:12:25, 00:45:22); the after-action / independent review shown only as read passages; the Vanity Fair article (00:40:55).

- DIA scan: "More tips at candaceowens.com" (00:45:05) is a DIA beat. "candaceowens.com" at 00:51:58 is a merch plug, not a DIA beat. The Latvian emails that corrected the operator's name (00:14:15) and the UVU staff emails (00:27:02) are tips received but do not use the scanned phrases. "Got this tip" (00:13:15) refers to the VPN workaround and is not a request for tips.

- Rejected claims (admission test): the host's characterization of the Andrew and Rachel Wilson types and TPUSA as gaudy or degenerate (00:08:02); "Turning Point doesn't feel clean anymore" (opinion); the Sheldon Adelson "purchasing the presidency vibe" (framing); the viewer comment that Erika is "nasty behind the scenes" (opinion); the Pentagon audit and Ukraine/Israel "laundromats" remarks (00:18:00, rhetoric); the host's statement that Laura Loomer is clinically insane (insult); the viewer suggestion that Gary Melton has a brain injury (insult); the Lady Lala comment about a Wyoming LLC and a search in Israel (unverifiable private anecdote); the viewer's dog and vet anecdote; the host's claim that Erika is frustrated she will not take over for Charlie (opinion).
- Ad reads (23:59-27:00, 41:15-43:25) for Dose, Paleo Valley, Nimi, Sentry H2O and American Financing are excluded.
